title: Speeding up a slow program
description:
Take a deliberately slow text report program and make it at least ten times faster, measuring every step.

```
before: 4.82 s
  locals for string.lower, string.gsub: 3.90 s
  table.concat instead of ..:          0.61 s
  one table lookup instead of a list scan: 0.21 s
after: 0.21 s (23x faster), same output
```

starter.main.lua:
local function slow_report(text)
    local out = ""
    local seen = {}
    for w in text:gmatch("%a+") do
        local found = false
        for _, s in ipairs(seen) do if s == string.lower(w) then found = true end end
        if not found then seen[#seen + 1] = string.lower(w); out = out .. string.lower(w) .. "\n" end
    end
    return out
end

print(#slow_report(string.rep("Lua is fun and tables are fun ", 200)))

hints: Change one thing at a time and measure after each, or you will not know which change helped (lesson 8.05).
The list scan inside the loop is the worst part: a set table finds a word in one step.
requirements: Keep the original as `slow_report` and write `fast_report`; check that both give exactly the same text.
Measure with `os.clock()` after each change and print the table above with your numbers.
Explain each change in a comment.
stretch: Try the same program in LuaJIT if you have it, and compare.
